rooms.comments:
A virtual room used to represent check locations that can be reached from multiple physical places on the map. For example, Weighted Belt can be purchased from Mort during Acts 1 and 2, or looted from his corpse a couple of rooms away during Act 3.

Archipelago represents this as a single canonical check location, so the multiple physical access paths need to converge on one logical location. Define one subroom in this virtual room for each such check.

For each physical origin, define a fake room transition in the origin room and its corresponding inverse transition in the appropriate virtual subroom. Apply the access requirements to the origin-side transition—for example, `act 1 OR act 2` for Mort's shop and `act 3` for his corpse—and link it to the corresponding transition in this room.

Mark the virtual-room inverse transition as `invalid`. Invalid transitions are not generated into the logical graph, preventing the virtual subroom from creating a route back to the origin or connecting otherwise unrelated physical origins through the virtual room.

Finally, place the single canonical AP check location—for example, Weighted Belt—in the corresponding virtual subroom. The result is one logical check that can be reached through any of its valid physical access paths without introducing false connectivity between those paths.
